title: Laozi (Li Er)
subtitle: A source figure of Daoist classicism and a later object of sacralisation
timeLabel: Traditionally placed in the late Spring and Autumn period; dates contested
shortSummary: Laozi is a recognisable gateway into Daoist classicism, but the Li Er biography, the sage-name Laozi, the formation of the Daodejing and the later Taishang Laojun image must remain distinct layers.
curatorialDescription: The museum treats Li Er as a name in early historiographical tradition, Laozi as a figure in intellectual and lineage traditions, and the authorship and formation of the Daodejing as a separate modelled question.
Laozi can connect an early source horizon with Tang reception and later sacralisation, but fame must not turn every Daoist text into a direct utterance by one person.
researchNote: Life dates and historicity are contested. The Shiji provides an early historiographical layer; textual attribution, the departure through Hangu Pass and later Taishang Laojun sacralisation require separate relations and sources.
